record.experiment_description:
OBJECTIVES:
This experiment attempted to expand the knowledge of environmental radiation at the 51.6 degree orbit, the location of the Mir station and future location of the International Space Station. Information on the shielding effects of the station and different methods of radiation dosimetry was also gathered. The data and associated analysis contributed to the establishment of a reliable database for the radiation environment in space.

APPROACH:
Two types of spectra were measured and compared: linear energy transfer (LET) and absorbed dose. The measurements for both spectra occurred inside six area passive dosimeters (APDs) that were flown to Mir via Shuttle mission STS-76 and placed at six different locations on Mir. LET spectra was measured using CR-39 PNTDs that were placed on the APDs. The CR-39 plates were etched with a NaOH solution and read out on an image digitizer system and analyzed. The absorbed spectra was measured using thermoluminescent detectors (TLDs) attached to the APDs. The flight data was compared with data read from background and calibration TLDs.

RESULTS:
By using identical APDs in the exact locations on Mir, changes in radiation levels over time were recorded and analyzed. The measured dose rates in the APDs ranged from 268 to 422 mGy/d, yielding an average of 324 mGy/d. The differences in the high and low values were most likely caused by shielding differences due to the individual APD placements on Mir. Also, secondary target fragments, generated by inelastic scattering of protons and alpha particles within the detector medium, contributed to the spread of values. The dose and dose equivalent rates were used to calculate the effective quality factor, which was determined to be about 9 for LETs 25 keV/mm. This value shows the significance of short-range high LET target fragments to dose equivalent. The shielding data is currently being used to model the APD measurements made in the Mir Core.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Comparison of Absorbed Doses and Mean Dose Rates in Six NASA 2/Mir21 Area Passive Dosimeters (APDs)
dataset_description:
This tables shows a comparison of total absorbed dose and absorbed dose rate as measured by both the University of San Francisco and Institute of Biomedical Problems (IBMP) thermoluminescent dosimeters.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Absorbed Doses and Mean Dose Rates Measured by the University of San Francisco Thermoluminescent Detectors (TLDs) During the NASA 4/Mir 23 Mission
dataset_description:
This table shows the total absorbed dose and mean dose rate for each of the TLDs deployed during the NASA 4 mission.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Absorbed Dose Measurents Made Using Thermoluminescent Detectors (TLDs) at Area Passive Dosimeter 2 (APD-2) Location
dataset_description:
This table shows the absorbed dose and absorbed dose rate measurements made using TLDs at the APD-2 location on Ceiling Panel No. 325 near the R-16 operational dosimeter, mean shielding = 44 g/cm2.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Equations Used for Determination of Dose Efficiency, Total Dose, and Total Dose Equivalent
dataset_description:
Image showing equations used to calculate dose efficiency, total dose, total dose equivalent, and average quality factor.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Mir External STD Platform Dose Rate Under Low Shielding
dataset_description:
Dose as a function of shielding depth measured on the external surface of Mir during the NASA 4/ Mir 23 and NASA 5/ Mir 24 missions. Also shown are measurements made at the same location in 1991 and a model calculation for the 1991 measurement.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Coordinates of Locations Inside the Mir Core Module for which Shielding Distributions Were Calculated.
dataset_description:
This table shows the locations inside the Mir Core Module for which shielding distributions were calculated. The locations are indicated using cartesian coordinates, where the origin (0,0,0) is located at the front of the adapter module, and the centerline of the station. The mean shielding density is also listed for each of the locations.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Final Reports for NASA Mir Experiment 9401620
dataset_description: These records represent the final reports for the NASA 2, 3, 4 and 5 missions, as well as a comprehensive report that covers all missions.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Altitude of the Mir Space Station
dataset_description:
This graph shows the altitude of the Mir Space Station as a function of time. On 4/15/97, Mir was boosted from a mean altitude of 385 km to 390 km.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Measured Dose Rates and Dose Equivalent Rates on the NASA 3/Mir 22 Mission
dataset_description:
This table shows the dose rates and dose equivalent rates as measured during the NASA 3/ Mir 22 mission (9/16/96 - 1/22/97, 127.2 days) using thermoluminescent detectors (TLDs) and CR-39 plastic nuclear track detectors (PNTDs), and contributions to total dose rates and dose equivalent rates form particles, including target fragments, of linear energy transfer (LET) greater than or equal to 5 keV/ micrometer. The location of the area passive dosimeters (APDs) and the mean quality factors are also listed.

Source: E. V. Benton and A. L. Frank. Environmental Radiation Measurements on Mir Station. Final report to NASA, Contract No. NCC2-893. Unpublished data.
